attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter. 'I believe' states his position; it is not a hedge.

semantics.note: The normalised wording matches the statement. The revenue-scale part can be observed. 'Masquerading' and 'the media is helping' are largely characterisation.

contract.note: The revenue reading (annualised, Q2 2025) is fair. The support condition stretches the claim: it requires the media to present current revenue as about $1T. An ordinary reader would take 'masquerading' as hype, valuation or spending implying a trillion-dollar industry. That makes support nearly impossible on terms the speaker never set.

evidence.note: Menlo's company release covers consumer AI spend only (about $12B). That is narrower than the claimed industry, so it can neither confirm nor refute an aggregate figure of about $50B.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no consistently scoped estimate of total generative AI revenue and no record of media representations. The only item is a narrower consumer-spend figure. The contract's media clause also reads the claim unfairly. The evidence does not settle either part.

attribution.note: The aside '(they won't)' is Zitron's own assertion in his newsletter.

semantics.note: 'They won't' is a firm negative forecast with a 2026 horizon. The quantity question that follows is separate, so 'build' means producing the chip at all.

contract.note: Counting functional fabricated silicon as 'build' is a fair ordinary reading. The speaker separates building from 'how many', and the contract does not require mass deployment.

evidence.note: OpenAI's dated disclosure of 2026-06-24 reports physical engineering samples of the jointly built chip running workloads, with the chip delivered by Broadcom. This is a company disclosure, but it describes a concrete physical event, as the contract's source rules allow.

reviews.rationale: The early-resolution rule is met. In June 2026 OpenAI disclosed functional engineering samples of the joint OpenAI–Broadcom accelerator running ML workloads, so the chip was built in 2026. Commercial scale is not required under the speaker's framing. The source is a company disclosure, not an independent finding.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter.

semantics.note: Narrowing the scope to the paid coding and search companies discussed is reasonable. 'Not real businesses' is normative and cannot be tested. Only the profitability assertion is factual.

contract.note: Company-level profit is the ordinary reading. The Q2 2025 window and the company universe are evaluator choices, and the speaker gave no accounting basis. The contract flags all of this appropriately.

evidence.note: The Base44 founder reports $189K profit in May 2025. This is self-reported and not tied to net income, and it is unclear whether Base44 is among 'these companies' discussed. It does not meet the contradiction condition.
TechCrunch (June 18, 2025) calls Base44 profitable, but this relies on the founder's own claims. It corroborates that the claim was available, not audited profit.

reviews.rationale: There is plausible counterevidence (Base44's founder-reported profit), but it is not on an established accounting basis and may fall outside the intended group. The packet has no complete financials for the group. The normative 'real businesses' part cannot be scored.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter.

semantics.note: 'So many people will see their retirements wrecked' is a firm forecast with no deadline. Context ties it to the predicted AI-bubble collapse.

contract.note: The plain reading of widespread, severe retirement damage caused by an AI collapse is fair. The contract correctly bars healthy accounts from disproving an open-ended forecast.

evidence.note: SBS reports Korean investors' retirement-pension losses in semiconductor ETFs during the July 2026 selloff. These are individual cases. They do not show widespread wrecked retirements or a full AI-collapse cause.
Seoul Economic Daily reports a -26% return on one chip ETF in one person's retirement account. Early buyers gained. This is not evidence of widespread severe impairment.
Fidelity's company data show US retirement balances rising through Q2 2026. That predates the July losses, and it cannot disprove an open-ended forecast.

reviews.rationale: No deadline was stated. The early-resolution rule requires a documented AI collapse together with widespread severe retirement damage, and that is not met. The Korean reports show isolated losses in concentrated investments without a representative scale or attribution. US data are context only.
